source_text:
πρόσωπον ὃ ἐνεδύσατο, τίς ἱκανὸς ἐλέγξαι; τίς ἱκανὸς ἀποκαλύψαι καὶ δεῖξαι ὅ τι
ἔνδον δράκων ἐστί; Καὶ μετ' ὀλίγα. Πρὸς τὴν μνήμην ἀνέ δραμον τῶν ἱερῶν
γραμμάτων, τούτῳ θεοπ νεύστῳ βιβλίῳ τοῦ Ἰὼβ ἐγκειμένων, καὶ ὡς ἐν σωματικῇ
διαπλάσει τὸ λίαν ἀνειδὲς καὶ ποικίλον κεκρυμμένον τῶν ἐπινοιῶν καὶ τῆς τῶν
ἔξωθεν προσωπείων ἀπαλλαγῆς, ἀπο γράφων τοῦ διαβόλου καὶ δαιμόνων ἀρχε
κάκου καὶ πονηρῶν. Φησὶ γάρ· Τίς ἀποκαλύ ψει πρόσωπον ἐνδύσεως αὐτοῦ; –Καὶ
ἐπεί περ ἔριζε τῆς ἔξωθεν φαινομένης ταύτης ποικιλίας, ὡς ἔκ τινος βάθους τῆς
ἀφανοῦς κακίας ἀνίσχουσι, ἐπενήνεκται τοῖς εἰρη μένοις καὶ ταῦτα· Τίς ἀποκαλύψει
πρόσωπον ἐνδύσεως αὐτοῦ, τουτέστι τίς ἱκανὸς εἰσελ θεῖν εἰς τὰ νοήματα τῆς
καρδίας αὐτοῦ, διότι συνεπτυγμένα τυγχάνουσι; ιδʹ, ιεʹ, Οὐ σαλευθήσεται, ἡ καρδία
αὐτοῦ 388 πέπηγεν ὡς λίθος, ἕστηκεν δὲ ὥσπερ ἄκ μων ἀνήλατος. Ἀπελιθώθη,
φησὶν, ἡ καρδία αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐκ ἐλαθῆναι δύναται· ἀλλ' ὅλος ἐστὶν ἀπεσ κληκὼς καὶ
ἰταμός· οὐκ ἐλαυνόμενος, οὐκ ἀκολουθῶν λόγῳ, οὐκ εἴκει· ὁ δὲ σκληρός ἐστιν,
ἀνήλατος, ἀνένδοτος. Καὶ εἴ τις ἀπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου ἀπέσπασε δύναμιν, καὶ τού του
δράκοντος αὐτὸς ἔχει τὴν καρδίαν ἀνή λατον καὶ οὐκ ἐλαυνομένην. Εἰ δέ τις χρυσός
ἐστιν ἀκολουθῶν τῷ λόγῳ, τῷ χρυσοχοϊκῷ οὗτος εἴκει ἕως ἂν γένηται πέταλον
χρυσοῦν, καὶ δέξηται τοὺς τύπους τῶν γραμμάτων τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, ᾧ ἡ
δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας αἰώνων. Ἀμήν. Κεφ. ΜΒʹ, ιʹ. Ἔδωκεν δὲ ὁ Κύριος διπλᾶ ὅσα ἦν
ἔμπροσθεν Ἰὼβ εἰς διπλασιασμόν. ιβʹ. Ὁ δὲ Κύριος εὐλόγησε τὰ ἔσχατα Ἰὼβ, ἢ τὰ
ἔμπροσθεν· ἦν δὲ τὰ κτήνην αὐ τοῦ, πρόβατα μύρια τετρακισχίλια, κάμη λοι
ἐξακισχίλιαι, ζεύγη βοῶν χίλια. ιγʹ. Γεννῶνται δὲ αὐτῷ υἱοὶ ἑπτὰ καὶ θυ γατέρες
τρεῖς. Εἰ πάντα τὰ ὅσα ἦν ἔμπροσθεν τῷ Ἰὼβ, διπλᾶ δέδωκεν ὁ Κύριος, μετὰ τὴν
pass_a_gloss: [The] face which he put on, who is sufficient to refute (expose)? who is sufficient to uncover and show what the dragon is inside? And after a few things. I ran up to the remembrance of the holy writings lying in this God-breathed book of Job, and, as in a bodily moulding, the very formless and varied hidden thing of the devices and of the riddance (putting off) of the outside masks, describing (participle, masculine singular, no stated subject), of the devil and of demons, the originator of evil, and wicked ones. For he (it) says: Who will uncover the face of his clothing? And since roots (read ῥίζαι for printed ἔριζε) of this variety appearing from outside, as from some depth of the unseen vice, rise up, these things also have been brought in addition to the things said: Who will uncover the face of his clothing, that is, who is sufficient to go into the thoughts of his heart, because they happen to be folded together? Labels: verses 14, 15 (KJV 41:23-24). It will not be shaken; his heart has been fixed like a stone, and stands like an anvil not beaten out. His heart, he says, was turned to stone, and is not able to be beaten out (driven, as metal); but he is wholly dried up hard and reckless; not being beaten out, not following reason, he does not give way; and he is hard, unmalleable, not yielding. And if someone drew power off from the devil, he himself also has the heart of this dragon, unmalleable and not being beaten out. But if someone is gold, following the word, this one gives way to the goldsmith's [craft] until he becomes a golden leaf, and receives the stamps of the letters of God, in Christ Jesus, to whom the glory into the ages of ages. Amen. Chapter 42, verse 10. And the Lord gave double the things which were before to Job, into doubling. Verse 12. And the Lord blessed the last things of Job rather than the earlier; and his beasts were sheep ten thousand four thousand, camels six thousand, yokes of oxen a thousand. Verse 13. And sons are born to him seven and daughters three. If all the things that were before to Job the Lord has given double, after the …
pass_b_english: The face that he put on: who is able to expose it? Who is able to uncover it and show what the dragon is within? And a little further on: I ran back to the memory of the sacred writings set down in this God-inspired book of Job, where, as in a bodily figure, he sketches what is exceedingly formless and many-sided and hidden in the schemes, and in the shedding of the outward masks, of the devil, the author of evil, and of the wicked demons. For it says: “Who will uncover the face of his garment?” (Job 41:13).

And since the roots of this variety that shows on the outside rise up as from some depth of unseen wickedness, these words too are added to what has been said: “Who will uncover the face of his garment?” That is: who is able to enter into the thoughts of his heart, since they are folded up together?

“It will not be shaken. His heart is set fast like a stone, and it stands like an anvil that cannot be beaten out” (Job 41:23-24). His heart, it says, has turned to stone and cannot be beaten out; he is wholly dried hard and headstrong. He is not beaten out, he does not follow reason, he does not yield; he is hard, unmalleable, unyielding. And if anyone has drawn power from the devil, he too has the heart of this dragon, unmalleable and not to be beaten out. But if anyone is gold, following the word, he yields to the goldsmith's art until he becomes a leaf of gold and receives the impressions of the letters of God, in Christ Jesus, to whom be glory to the ages of ages. Amen.

“And the Lord gave Job double all that he had before, for doubling” (Job 42:10). “And the Lord blessed the last days of Job more than the first; and his livestock were fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen” (Job 42:12). “And seven sons and three daughters are born to him” (Job 42:13). lemmas.gloss: anvil not to be beaten out

choices.choice: ἐπεί περ ἔριζε ... ἀνίσχουσι read as ἐπείπερ ῥίζαι ... ἀνίσχουσι ('since the roots ... rise up'): ἔριζε ('was contending') has no sense here and the plural verb needs a plural subject. A reviewer should check the PG page (col. 387-388) for this word.

Πρὸς τὴν μνήμην ἀνέδραμον ... ἀπογράφων ... πονηρῶν has a main verb (ἀνέδραμον) and an unattached masculine participle ἀπογράφων; taken as the author of the book ('he sketches'). τοῦ διαβόλου ... ἀρχεκάκου is singular (the devil, the author of evil), πονηρῶν goes with δαιμόνων. The old bracket '[the sentence is corrupt and has no main verb]' was wrong and is removed. ἀπαλλαγῆς may be a misprint for ἐναλλαγῆς ('exchange of masks'); rendered as printed.
Οὐ σαλευθήσεται, ἡ καρδία αὐτοῦ πέπηγεν: the comma closes LXX verse 14 (KJV 41:23 'they cannot be moved'); the heart begins verse 15. Old English made the heart the subject of 'will not be shaken'.
ἀνήλατος, ἐλαθῆναι, ἐλαυνόμενος (ἐλαύνω, to beat out metal) rendered 'unmalleable', 'beaten out'; old 'not driven' lost the image that the gold sentence completes.
The 42:12 lemma has sheep, camels and oxen but not the she-asses; translated as given. τὰ κτήνην is a print slip for τὰ κτήνη.
'Chapter 42, verse 10:' etc. replaced by the work's convention: quoted lemma followed by the English reference.
